column1: # OmacVM features: the one list that the setup questions, `omacvm features`,
# `omacvm enable/disable`, the VM installer (guest/install.sh) and the checks
# follow. One feature per line, tab-separated:
#   name  default (on|off|notch: on with a notch|laptop: on with a battery, not on Parallels)  sides (mac,vm)  tags  needs  title  summary
# Tags: experimental, slow (adds build/update time), notch (needs a MacBook with a notch),
# laptop (needs a Mac with a battery), not-parallels (Parallels does it itself),

column7: the Mac's Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, audio, Night Shift and media keys in Omarchy's bar
Omarchy's wallpaper becomes the Mac's, following the theme
3/4-finger swipes and pinch in Omarchy while it is full screen (⌃⌥⌘ Esc hands them back to macOS)
two-finger scrolling with your Mac's own acceleration and momentum, passed through
Omarchy's bar beside the MacBook's notch
the clock at the far right of the bar, formatted like the Mac's menu bar
Linux apps and video calls in the browser see it as Mac Camera; it is on only while one of them uses it (UTM and VMware Fusion: through OmacVM Bridge, installed for it also with the Bridge off)
its charge and charging state in Omarchy's bar, as on a laptop (UTM, VMware Fusion, OmacVM.app; Parallels shows it itself)
Omarchy's own, after idle in the VM (off: the Mac's lock protects the VM)
straight into Omarchy, without its login screen
Arch Linux ARM's kernel with transparent huge pages and MGLRU, for memory-heavy work (about 10 minutes per build and update)

the VM on macOS's own VM network (vmnet, as Parallels and UTM) instead of QEMU's built-in one: faster to and from the Mac, steady latency, an address of its own; a small system service, so macOS asks for your password once (OmacVM.app only)
